title: Parallel Rank-Adaptive Higher Order Orthogonal Iteration
problem: Tucker decomposition is useful for compressing large tensors, but existing algorithms have fixed rank requirements that may not match actual data compressibility. Rank selection and tensor decomposition at scale are computationally expensive.
motivation: Rank-adaptive decomposition can automatically select appropriate ranks to meet approximation error targets, potentially achieving better compression ratios than fixed-rank methods like STHOSVD.
method: Rank-adaptive modification to HOOI (Higher Order Orthogonal Iteration) that determines Tucker ranks adaptively subject to fixed approximation error targets. Optimizations reduce per-iteration cost. Parallel implementation using thousands of cores for large dense datasets.
key_novelty: Parallel rank-adaptive HOOI enabling automatic rank determination with competitive or superior compression ratios compared to fixed-rank methods like STHOSVD.
contributions: Rank-adaptive HOOI algorithm with fixed approximation error targets
Optimizations reducing cost per HOOI iteration
Parallel implementation scaling to thousands of cores
Demonstration that HOOI achieves better compression ratios than STHOSVD in high-compression regimes
82x faster Tucker decomposition than STHOSVD for 3D fluid-flow datasets
50% better compression ratio on 3D fluid-flow simulation data
baselines: Sequentially Truncated Higher Order Singular Value Decomposition (STHOSVD)
limitations: Evaluation limited to three scientific simulation datasets; generalization to other tensor types not explored.
primary_theme: Efficient tensor compression for scientific data
